sector_model: restaurant operator: restaurant margin, comparable sales and traffic, commodity (beef) and labor inflation, unit growth, capex, lease liabilities; nonfinancial FCF with leases shown separately
thesis: Texas Roadhouse (steakhouse chain, company and franchise units) grew Q3 2026 revenue 9.5% to 1.573B and diluted EPS 8.6% to 1.36; nine-month operating cash flow 585.9M less capex 314.4M left 271.5M of free cash flow while it paid 147.9M dividends and repurchased 84.2M of stock, with only 50M revolver debt against 141.4M cash. After falls of 2.4% on 11-05 and 4.1% on 11-06 to 183.88, market cap is about 12.07B: roughly 27x annualized nine-month EPS (5.08 x 4/3 = 6.77, an approximation because Q4 2025 was not read) and an annualized free cash flow yield near 3.0%.
counterthesis: Quarter-to-date company comparable sales slowed to +1.5% (Q3 4.3%, nine months 5.9%) including about 1% menu price, so traffic is likely negative; the CEO said traffic softened late in the quarter. Nine-month restaurant margin fell to 15.8% from 16.0% as commodity inflation ran 5.0% (about half of food cost is beef, guided about 5.0% for the year) and wage inflation 3.9%. Net income grew only 4.3% in nine months against 11.2% revenue growth. Capex guidance rose to about 440M and store week growth is 5.0% to 5.5%, so free cash flow is thin for a 27x multiple. Lease liabilities are 1.07B and not in the debt figure. The stock still trades at a premium multiple despite the two day drop, and the cause of the fall (the guidance and quarter-to-date comps) is now identified from the release but not the call.
invalidation: Company comparable sales turning negative for two quarters; restaurant margin below 14% for a quarter; beef inflation above 8%; capex or lease obligations rising faster than operating cash flow; franchise comps diverging sharply from company comps.
